result.title: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
result.summary: Tool-augmented medical agents treat whatever their tools return as evidence. We show that this default is costly: medical tools fail silently, and a frozen reasoner cannot ignore what enters its context, so many cases it would have answered correctly are flipped to wrong once tool outputs are added. We call this evidence hijacking. $\mathcal{V}$-information explains the phenomenon: the reasoner has lost the option to ignore, so a tool output can carry negative usable information, and moving the decision of what to keep outside the reasoner restores that option. The theory further shows that part of any filtering gain comes merely from letting the reasoner see less, and only selection by content lets it see better. Building on this, we recast tool-augmented reasoning as evidence governance, which separates deciding what counts as evidence from the reasoner that answers, and propose context-independent evidence governance (CIEG), the first medical agent framework that rules, after acquisition, on whether each individual tool output may enter as evidence. Every tool output is written as a card that can be checked against the raw input; an independent checker that sees only the input and the cards decides which cards become evidence; and the reasoner answers from the admitted cards alone, with no training anywhere. On medical question answering, fundus glaucoma screening, and chest X-ray pneumonia classification, it achieves the highest accuracy among models of comparable scale, and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art tool-using agents and multi-agent systems built on the same backbone at lower cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出工具增强医疗 agent 把工具输出无条件当作证据会导致「证据劫持」，即本可答对的病例因错误工具输出被翻转，并用 V-information 解释；据此提出 CIEG 框架，把每个工具输出写成可对照原始输入核验的卡片，由只看输入与卡片的独立 checker 裁定其能否作为证据，reasoner 仅凭准入卡片作答，无需训练，在医疗问答、眼底青光眼筛查与胸片肺炎分类上取得较高准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 与关注视觉证据筛选、证据是否被真正使用以及「看得更少反而更好」的收益归因直接相关，其区分内容筛选增益与单纯缩减上下文的思路可供核查，并可能用于 LVR 中视觉旁路与工具输出准入的分析。
